policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV quotes a nominal sentence in direct discourse, 'saith, Jesus is anathema', with the copula supplied and Jesus as its subject; that is the nominative Ἰησοῦς, not the accusative Ἰησοῦν of an indirect construction.

Same construction in the second half: ASV 'can say, Jesus is Lord' is a quoted nominal clause with Jesus as subject and Lord as predicate, matching nominative Κύριος Ἰησοῦς rather than accusative Κύριον Ἰησοῦν.
ASV 'but the same God' renders the adversative δέ; the WH reading καὶ ὁ would give 'and the same God', as ASV in fact writes where καί stands elsewhere in the series.
ASV supplies no verb of its own here ('but the same God, who worketh all things in all'); an explicit ἐστιν and its absence are rendered identically in English, and no ASV note is mapped to the unit.

A connective δέ in the list of gifts. ASV's 'and to another' is distributed over the series without tracking the Greek particles, so its presence or absence at this item is not distinguished in the English.

Same connective δέ. ASV writes 'and to another gifts of healings', but it uses the same 'and to another' where no δέ stands and omits it where δέ does stand (v.10), so the English does not decide the particle.
ASV distinguishes the two phrases of the verse: 'in the same Spirit' for αὐτῷ earlier, then 'in the one Spirit' here, which renders ἑνὶ and not the RP αὐτῷ.
Connective δέ within the list of gifts; ASV's uniform 'and to another' is a stylistic English linkage across the series and does not distinguish presence from absence of the particle.
Connective δέ; nothing in ASV's 'and to another prophecy' answers to the particle as against its absence, and no mapped textual note bears on it.
Connective δέ; ASV's 'and to another discernings of spirits' renders the item, not the particle, which is untranslatable as a distinction here.

Connective δέ. ASV writes 'to another divers kinds of tongues' with no 'and' at all, though δέ stands in some editions here, which shows the English connectives do not track the particles; the unit is not decided.
Connective δέ; ASV's 'and to another the interpretation of tongues' does not distinguish the particle from its absence, and the only note on the verse is a greek_gloss on 'miracles'.
A word-order variant between πολλὰ and ἔχει; ASV 'hath many members' fixes the English order regardless, so neither Greek sequence is distinguished.
ASV reads simply 'all the members of the body, being many'; the RP addition τοῦ ἑνός would give 'of the one body', and ASV has no such 'one' here, nor an italicized supply.
ASV 'were we all baptized into one body' renders the εἰς that both readings carry before ἓν σῶμα; an added εἰς after πάντες produces no further English word, so the unit is not distinguished.
νυνὶ and νῦν are the same adverb; ASV 'But now' renders either, and no mapped note bears on the form.

μέν is routinely left untranslated in ASV; 'But now they are many members, but one body' shows no correlative 'indeed', which is equally what the omission would yield, so the English does not decide it.

ASV 'our comely parts have no need' leaves the verb without a complement; the NIV reading adds τιμῆς, which would give 'have no need of honor', and no such phrase (or italicized supply) stands in ASV.
Active ὑστεροῦντι and middle ὑστερουμένῳ are alike rendered 'that lacked'; ASV's wording does not distinguish the voice, and no mapped note addresses it.
ASV has the singular 'that there should be no schism in the body', matching σχίσμα; the RP plural σχίσματα would require 'no schisms/divisions'.
ASV 'And whether one member suffereth ... or one member is honored' renders the correlative εἴτε ... εἴτε; Treg's εἴ τι would give a conditional 'if anything', which ASV does not have.
ASV writes 'or one member is honored' with the numeral present and unitalicized in the second clause as well as the first, answering to ἓν μέλος rather than bare μέλος.

ἔπειτα and εἶτα are both rendered 'then', as ASV's 'then miracles, then gifts of healings' shows; the ASV notes on this verse are a greek_gloss and an alternative_rendering, neither of which bears on the reading.
ASV 'desire earnestly the greater gifts' renders the comparative of μέγας, μείζονα; RP's κρείττονα would give 'better' rather than 'greater'.
